chapters.title: 13.1 Real-World Capstone Project
chapters.overviewText: The capstone is a public, CI-gated Cypress suite against a Bizlevate-like HRM (or a faithful demo): session login, leave submit/approve, at least one cy.origin SSO stub or real IdP, a component test for a form, axe on a modal, grep-tagged smoke, and GitHub Actions with artifacts. Multi-tab PDF is handled with href/request, not switchToTab. Native mobile is explicitly out of scope (Appium).
chapters.why: Employers hire evidence. A kitchen-sink clone of example.cypress.io is weaker than a domain suite that shows architecture judgment (origin, CT vs E2E, no fake WebKit).
chapters.when: After Parts 0–12, when you need one project that you can talk through in an interview for 15 minutes.

practical.scenario: You must design and implement a capstone that would survive a staff-engineer code review at Bizlevate.
practical.pass: You ship a repo with README, data-cy, cy.session, one origin (or documented stub), CT for LeaveRequestForm, @smoke in GHA, Mochawesome or artifacts, and a written 'what we did not test' (tabs, WebKit, native).
practical.fail: You record a UI-login every test, sleep-based suite against the Cypress kitchen sink, and claim mobile native coverage.

chapters.customSummary:
- Domain suite (leave/payroll/roles), not only example.cypress.io.
- Must show: session, intercept or request, CT vs E2E, grep smoke, GHA action, artifacts.
- Must show judgment: cy.origin args, no switchToTab, no built-in visual, no Trace Viewer, Appium for native.
- README = the interview script.
- Playwright/Selenium capstones can coexist — say why Cypress was the right tool for this app.
chapters.contentMarkdown:
## Scope a capstone that fits a week, not a quarter

**In:**

- App: Bizlevate HRM demo or your clone (employees, leave, a manager queue). If you cannot use the real app, use a public HRM-like demo **plus** a README that maps features.
- E2E: login via `cy.session`, employee submits leave, manager approves, list reflects status (intercept or real API — say which).
- Cross-origin: either a real IdP in `cy.origin('https://...', { args }, cb)` or a documented fake IdP origin. Show `args` and a yielded value once.
- CT: `LeaveRequestForm` zero-balance + submit disabled (9.5).
- a11y: `cypress-axe` on the leave modal (9.7).
- Org: `@smoke` / `@regression` with grep plugin (10.1).
- CI: `cypress-io/github-action`, Chrome, wait-on, screenshots on failure (11.1, 11.8).

**Out (and say so in README):**

- Native iOS app — Appium.
- Safari/WebKit first-class — Playwright if needed.
- Two live tabs — href/`cy.request` only.
- Visual AI — plugin or skip, do not pretend `cy.screenshot` diffs.

## Suggested spec map

| Spec | Tags | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `login.cy.ts` | `@smoke` | session only after first |
| `leave-submit.cy.ts` | `@smoke @leave` | intercept balance |
| `leave-approve.cy.ts` | `@leave` | two sessions (employee, manager) |
| `sso.cy.ts` | `@okta @nightly` | `cy.origin` + args |
| `payslip-link.cy.ts` | `@payroll` | href + `cy.request` PDF |
| `LeaveRequestForm.cy.tsx` | CT | props matrix |

## Definition of done

- `npx cypress run --browser chrome --env grepTags=@smoke` < 6 minutes locally.
- GHA badge green on main.
- No `cy.wait(n)` without a comment that you are ashamed of.
- One paragraph in README: Cypress vs Playwright vs Selenium *for this product*.

Interview line: "My capstone is an HRM journey suite: session, origin with args, CT for the form, smoke in GitHub Actions. I did not fake tabs or native mobile."

chapters.title: 13.2 Portfolio Building
chapters.overviewText: A Cypress portfolio is a GitHub repo a stranger can clone: README with architecture decisions, how to run, CI badge, sample report/screenshot, and honest limits. One excellent HRM project beats ten tutorial repos. Link CT and E2E. Do not commit cypress.env.json secrets, videos of real payroll, or node_modules.
chapters.why: Recruiters open the README first. Cypress vs Playwright vs Appium sentences in that README do more than a certificate (14.6).
chapters.when: When the capstone is green, before you apply, and when you add Playwright/Appium repos — they should cross-link.

practical.scenario: You have a working capstone and a Playwright Python repo. You need a portfolio that looks like one engineer, not two random tutorials.
practical.pass: You publish the Cypress HRM repo with README (architecture + run + CI), hide secrets, add a short 'related: Playwright / Appium' section, and pin it on GitHub.
practical.fail: You push .env with passwords and a README that only says npm install.

chapters.customSummary:
- README: what the app is, how to run, CI, what is not covered (WebKit, tabs, native).
- Evidence: GHA badge, HTML report or screenshots in docs/, not a 200MB video in git.
- Secrets never committed; use env examples.
- Cross-link Playwright + Appium as breadth (13.4).
- Quality over count — one domain suite wins.
chapters.contentMarkdown:
## README outline (steal this)

1. **Problem** — HRM leave/payroll needs E2E + CT.
2. **Why Cypress** — JS frontend team, CT, in-page intercepts. Why *not* only Cypress — no WebKit, no tabs, native is Appium.
3. **How to run** — Node version, `npm ci`, `npm run start`, `npx cypress open`, CI command with grep.
4. **Architecture** — `cy.session`, fixtures, grep tags, origin helper with `args`.
5. **CI** — link to the GitHub Action workflow file (`cypress-io/github-action`).
6. **Limits** — PDF new tab tested via `cy.request`; no Trace Viewer; visual not in OSS core.

## What to show besides code

- A 60-second GIF of the App time-travel on a failed command (not a 40-minute 4K video).
- Mochawesome HTML hosted as GitHub Pages **if** it contains no PII (two-part merge, 11.6).
- Issues/PRs on your own repo showing you fixed flake (12.3) — process evidence.

## Hygiene

`cypress.env.json`, `videos/`, real employee exports: gitignore. Provide `cypress.env.json.example`. Never commit `CYPRESS_RECORD_KEY`.

## Versus a Playwright-only or Selenium-only portfolio

If you already have Playwright+Python, the Cypress repo should **not** clone the same tests line-for-line. Show CT, grep plugin, `cy.origin` args — the Cypress-shaped skills. A Selenium/JUnit repo still helps for enterprises that live on Grid; cross-link it as "WebDriver family + Appium" rather than competing with Cypress for the same screenshots.

Playwright portfolios usually show `trace.zip` and WebKit; Cypress portfolios should show the App GUI and CT. Interviewers who know both will ask why you chose each (Appendix A).

Interview line: "The README states why Cypress, how CI runs smoke, and what I refused to fake — tabs, WebKit, native. Playwright and Selenium repos are linked as breadth, not duplicates."

chapters.title: 13.3 Interview Prep
chapters.overviewText: Interview answers for Cypress are architecture sentences with a Bizlevate example, not command lists. Drill: command queue vs Promises, cy.origin args/return, no switchToTab, includeShadowDom, CT vs E2E, no built-in visual, cypress-axe, parallel = machines, no first-class WebKit, no Trace Viewer, retries hide flake, grep plugin, GitHub action, cypress/browsers, Sorry Cypress/Currents, Mochawesome two-part, cy.task vs cy.log, Appium for native.
chapters.why: A whiteboard 'compare Cypress and Playwright' is the most common senior screen. This chapter is the cheat sheet you earned in Parts 0–12.
chapters.when: The week before interviews, and after any chapter you could not explain to a rubber duck.

practical.scenario: An interviewer says: 'SSO, a PDF tab, Safari, and a native app — how do you test Bizlevate?' You have 8 minutes.
practical.pass: You split tools: cy.origin+args for SSO, href/request for PDF, Playwright or cloud Safari for WebKit, Appium for native, Cypress CT for the form, GHA+grep for CI. You never say Cypress does all four.
practical.fail: You recite cy.get/cy.click and say Cypress is just faster Selenium.

chapters.customSummary:
- Lead with execution model (in-page vs driver), then limits, then substitutes.
- Memorize the must-teach list in this chapter's drills.
- Prefer one HRM story over ten APIs.
- Code pairing: write a session+intercept spec, not a sleep.
- Compare Playwright/Selenium without trashing them — you might need all three.
chapters.contentMarkdown:
## Drill questions (answer out loud)

**Why aren't Cypress commands Promises?** Queue + retry-ability. `await cy.get` is wrong.

**SSO?** `cy.origin(url, { args }, cb)`; args serializable; yield to return data. Playwright: transparent. Selenium: transparent (`get` on the IdP URL).

**PDF new tab?** No `cy.switchToTab`. Assert href or `cy.request`. Playwright: popup Page. Selenium: window handles.

**Shadow DOM?** `includeShadowDom` or `.shadow()`. Playwright pierces open shadow by default. Selenium: `getShadowRoot()`.

**CT vs E2E?** `cy.mount` isolation vs real journeys. Playwright CT exists (JS); Selenium has none.

**Visual?** No built-in matcher. Plugin/SaaS. Playwright `toHaveScreenshot`. Selenium: plugin/SaaS.

**a11y?** `cypress-axe` / axe-core. `injectAxe` then `checkA11y`.

**Parallel?** Machines sharding specs, one browser each — not Chrome+Firefox in one process. Playwright workers; Selenium Grid.

**Safari?** No first-class WebKit.

**Trace?** Cypress has no Trace Viewer. Video/PNG; Cloud Debug/Replay paid. Playwright `trace.zip`.

**Retries?** Hide flake. Command retry ≠ test retry.

**Tags?** Grep plugin, not native.

**CI?** `cypress-io/github-action`, `cypress run`, wait-on.

**Docker?** `cypress/browsers` / `included`.

**No Cloud?** Sorry Cypress / Currents / Mochawesome two-part.

**Logs in CI?** `cy.task` not `cy.log`.

**Native mobile?** Appium — same answer if they say Playwright or Selenium.

## Live coding expectations

```js
cy.session('emp', () => { /* request or UI */ });
cy.intercept('GET', '/api/leave', { fixture: 'leave.json' }).as('leave');
cy.visit('/leave');
cy.wait('@leave');
cy.get('[data-cy=new-request]').click();
```

Talk while you type: intercept **before** visit, session before visit, data-cy. If they ask you to `await` it, explain the queue. If they ask for `driver.switchTo()`, explain 9.3.

## Behavioral

"Tell me about flake" → 9.13 + 12.3 story with a metric (retries, then a fix).
"Disagreement on tool" → 9.2 senior split Cypress / Playwright / Selenium.

Interview line: "I explain the iframe architecture, then I map each Bizlevate risk to origin, request, Playwright, Selenium Grid, or Appium."

chapters.title: 13.4 Career Positioning
chapters.overviewText: Position Cypress as the JS/TS in-browser E2E+CT tool for frontend-owned quality, not as a religion. Pair it with Playwright (multi-engine, traces, other languages) and Appium (native). Titles: QA Automation, SDET, frontend engineer who tests. Cypress Cloud knowledge is orchestration, not a personality.
chapters.why: Hiring managers hear 'I only do Cypress' as a ceiling. Breadth with honest limits is the senior brand this manual trained.
chapters.when: Writing LinkedIn/headline, choosing the next learning track, and answering 'where do you see yourself.'

practical.scenario: You are applying to a company that uses Playwright Python and has a native app, but your deepest suite is Cypress HRM.
practical.pass: You present Cypress as web/CT depth, Playwright as already-learned or next, Appium as the native plan — one quality engineer, several interfaces.
practical.fail: You argue they must rewrite Playwright into Cypress to hire you.

chapters.customSummary:
- Brand: in-browser E2E + CT + CI, with architectural honesty.
- Portfolio breadth: Cypress (JS) + Playwright + Appium > any single tool.
- Paths: SDET vs QA automation vs frontend-with-tests; Cloud/CI leans platform.
- Do not market Cloud AI as your skill core.
- Domain (HR/payroll) is a differentiator equal to the tool.
chapters.contentMarkdown:
## A headline that does not lie

"SDET — Cypress (E2E+CT) for JS apps, Playwright for multi-engine/web scale, Appium for native. HR/payroll domain."

Not: "Cypress ninja | AI testing guru | 10x automation."

## How the paths use this manual

| Path | Lean on |
|---|---|
| Frontend engineer | CT, App time-travel, intercepts, data-cy advocacy |
| QA Automation | Journeys, grep smoke, reports, flake process |
| SDET | origin/session architecture, GHA, Docker, sharding |
| Platform/DevOps | `cypress/browsers`, artifacts, Cloud vs Sorry Cypress |

## Tool politics

You can prefer Cypress's GUI and still recommend Playwright for Safari or tabs (9.2). That recommendation *is* seniority. Selenium still exists in Java enterprises — translating 9.16 is billable. Telling a TestNG shop to "just Cypress" without a JS skill plan is how migrations die.

Appium sits beside all three web tools. Native HRM work does not become Cypress because you are a Cypress person.

## What not to over-index

- Official Cypress certificates (14.6) without a repo.
- Cloud AI demos (11.4).
- Record-and-playback Studio as your framework.

## A 12-month skill map

1. Capstone (13.1) green on GitHub Actions.
2. One Playwright WebKit or trace-debugging story so you are not single-engine.
3. Appium hello-world if the company has a store app — even a sample APK.
4. Optional: read a Selenium Grid diagram so you can talk to the existing Java team.

Interview line: "I'm a quality engineer. Cypress is my strongest web/CT tool. I use Playwright and Selenium where the architecture or the org requires it, and Appium for native."
